newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stocks finish weak amid record volumes.
newsitem.headline: S.African stocks finish weak amid record volumes.

text.p: Thwarting pre-Christmas holiday fever, South African shares set new record turnover on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange of 1.07 billion rand, including a large overnight asset swap, dealers said.
The previous record was 999.7 million rand on April 6, 1996.
Dealers said a large asset swap took place on Wednesday night, contributing about 300 million rand to overall turnover.
But, despite shrugging off Wall Street's heavy losses and stifling their morning drop, industrials and all-shares finished the day weak as a falling rand took its toll.
The rand lost nearly nine cents of its value on the day, pulled down by dollar demand out of London and then strong local importer demand, "catching some people sleeping", dealers said.
Gold shares remained stuck in their tight range and dipped to close slightly weaker as a listless bullion price failed to move them.

Overall, dealers were looking for a firmer market on Friday. They said unit-trusts would start window-dressing stocks and that futures players would want to close off a lot of open reverse arbitrage positions ahead of the close-out on Tuesday.
Industrials ended 37.1 points down at 7,814.7, all-shares were off 32.1 at 6,607 and golds dipped 8.9 to 1,533.2.
